title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the Lefschetz-type standard conjecture C(X) (in the Bombay paper this is B(X)). It says that the Lefschetz operator Λ_X, the 'inverse' of L_X in the sl2 sense, is induced by an algebraic correspondence. The page is an isolated handwritten sheet; the neighbouring pages 40 and 42 are unrelated typescripts. The page sets up an inductive reduction of C(X) along hyperplane sections. Notation: X is smooth projective of dimension n, φ: Y ↪ X a smooth hyperplane section, φ^* restriction, φ_* the Gysin map, L_X = φ_*φ^* = cup with the hyperplane class, L_Y = φ^*(hyperplane class).

(1) Assume C(Y). Then C(X) is equivalent to the following. For i ≤ n−1, restriction φ^i: H^i(X) → H^i(Y) is injective by weak Lefschetz. A canonical left inverse ψ^i: H^i(Y) → H^i(X) is given by Λ_X φ_* restricted to H^i(Y). The condition is that this left inverse is induced by an algebraic class, i.e. that 'Λ_X φ_* is algebraic'.

(2) Λ_X φ_* is a correspondence from Y to X. Its class lies in Σ_i H^{2(n−1)−i}(Y) ⊗ H^i(X) = H^{2(n−1)}(X×Y). Since m = dim(X×Y) = 2n−1, this is H^{m−1}(X×Y), one step below the middle.

(3) Key trick. The Lefschetz operator of X×Y is L_X⊗1 + 1⊗L_Y. Applied to the class of u = Λ_Xφ_*, it gives the class of L_X u + u L_Y = L_XΛ_Xφ_* + Λ_Xφ_*L_Y. By the projection formula φ_*L_Y = L_Xφ_*, so this equals (Λ_XL_X + L_XΛ_X)φ_*. Grothendieck then rewrites this, using the sl2 relation [Λ,L] = Σ(weights)·p_i^X (crossed-out attempt) and the fact p_m^X φ_* = 0. The result is an expression of the form (φ_*Λ_Yφ^* + id_X)φ_*, built from φ_*, φ^*, Λ_Y (algebraic by C(Y)) and identities/projectors. Hence L_{X×Y}(class of Λ_Xφ_*) is algebraic.

(4) The Lefschetz conjecture A^0(X×Y) is now applied in degree m−1. It says that a class ξ ∈ H^{m−1} with Lξ algebraic is itself algebraic. So Λ_Xφ_* is algebraic. This gives C(X) ⇔ [C(Y) and A^0(X×Y)].

(5) Iterating along a flag of smooth hyperplane sections X ⊃ Y ⊃ Z ⊃ T ⊃ … down to curves (where C holds) gives:
C(X) ⇐ A^0(X×Y) ∧ A^0(Y×Z) ∧ A^0(Z×T) ∧ …
The final remark, 'with discussion of the necessary hypotheses of non-singularity' ('avec discussion des hypothèses de non-singularité'), flags that the smoothness of the sections needs care.

Purpose: reduce the Lefschetz-type standard conjecture to the 'A' (hard-Lefschetz-converse) conjecture in a single degree (just below the middle) on products of a variety with its hyperplane section.
errors: The middle computation is garbled and partly crossed out. As written, '(Λ_XL_X + L_XΛ_X)φ_*' passes to 'Λ_XL_Xφ_* = (φ_*Λ_Yφ^* + id_X)φ_*' without a justified step. The identity relating ΛL+LΛ, or ΛL alone, on the image of φ_* to φ_*Λ_Yφ^* is asserted, not proved. The weight/sign conventions are also missing.

The argument appears to use the Künneth/weight projectors p_i^X (crossed-out line, and 'p_m^X φ_* = 0'). Their algebraicity is itself part of the standard conjectures (C/B ⇒ Künneth). Whether the induction hypothesis supplies them is not made explicit, so this is a possible gap.
The equivalence 'C(X) ⇔ [C(Y) and A^0(X×Y)]' only clearly yields ⇐ from the computation. The ⇒ direction (C(X) ⇒ C(Y)) is not argued on the page. The final chain is correctly stated with ⇐ only.
Line 3 of the machine transcription has Λ_Xφ^* where the image clearly means Λ_Xφ_* (or Λ_Xφ_* restricted to H^i(Y)).

ideas.what: Under C(Y), C(X) is equivalent to algebraicity of the canonical left inverse Λ_Xφ_* of restriction H^i(X)→H^i(Y), i ≤ n−1.
ideas.modern_name: Hyperplane-section reduction of the Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1968 Bombay 'Standard conjectures'), Kleiman (1968 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures')
ideas.where_published: Possibly Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), §4 remarks on stability of B under hyperplane sections. Kleiman 1968/1994 discusses related reductions.

ideas.what: Viewing Λ_Xφ_* as a class in H^{m−1}(X×Y), m = dim X×Y, and computing L_{X×Y} of it as (ΛL+LΛ)φ_* via L_X⊗1+1⊗L_Y and the projection formula. Algebraicity then follows from the converse-Lefschetz conjecture A on X×Y in degree m−1.
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of B(X) to A(X×Y) in degree just below the middle (sl2 trick on product with hyperplane section)
ideas.where_published: Possibly Grothendieck 1969 (Bombay) or Kleiman 1968 §2-4. Exact form unsure.

ideas.what: Iterating along a flag X ⊃ Y ⊃ Z ⊃ … of smooth hyperplane sections: C(X) follows from A^0 on the successive products X×Y, Y×Z, Z×T, ….
ideas.modern_name: Inductive reduction of the Lefschetz standard conjecture to A-conjectures on products of consecutive hyperplane sections

missed.claim: This is an explicit chain reduction: C(X) ⇐ ∧_k A^0(X_k × X_{k+1}) along a flag of smooth hyperplane sections. It reduces Lefschetz-type standard conjecture B for X to the converse-Lefschetz conjecture in a single degree (m−1) on products of consecutive members of the flag. I am not certain this precise 'flag' formulation appears in print. Grothendieck's published account states stability properties of B, and Kleiman gives related equivalences; this exact chain may be an unpublished variant.
missed.quote: C(X) ⟸ (A°(X×Y) et A°(Y×Z) et A°(Z×T) ---) X⊃Y⊃Z⊃T--
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It localizes the Lefschetz standard conjecture to one cohomological degree on varieties of odd dimension 2k−1 of a special shape (X_k × X_{k+1}). That could be relevant to current partial results on the Lefschetz standard conjecture, e.g. for specific classes of varieties or via the Hodge-theoretic (characteristic 0) approach. Probably known to specialists in substance.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuine working sketch of a standard-conjecture reduction (the sl2 trick on X×Y in degree m−1), closely matching material Grothendieck and Kleiman published in 1968-69. The flag-iterated form may be a slightly different packaging than the published one, but the ideas are known to specialists. The computation on the page is also incomplete.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the image reads 'l'homom. ψ^i_Σ : H^i(Y) → H^i(X), inverse à gauche [left inverse] de' — the map is named ψ (left inverse of φ^i), not φ^i_*.
Line 3: 'Λ_X φ^* | H^i(Y)' should be 'Λ_X φ_* | H^i(Y)'.
The phrase 'ou encore, i.e.' is just 'ou encore,' introducing the boxed condition 'Λ_X φ_* est algébrique'.
'Or ... L_{X×Y}(Λ_Xφ_*) correspond à' is followed by the operator 'L_X ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ L_Y' ('correspond à' / 'correspond par'), giving the next line 'i.e. Λ_Xφ_*L_Y + L_XΛ_Xφ_* = …'.
Final lines: 'X ⊃ Y ⊃ Z ⊃ T -- une suite de sections hyperplanes, avec discussion des hypothèses de non-singularité' (the last words are 'hypothèses ... non-singularité', not 'non singulières').
The page number at bottom left is 41.
